title: October's strongest meteor shower peaks Oct. 21. How Nevadans can see
excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks tonight, Oct. 21. Here's how Nevadans can see it.
content:
Oct. 21, 2026, 6:00 a.m. PT

Nevada meteor hunters have an astronomical autumnal treat to look forward to this evening. The Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak tonight, Wednesday, Oct. 21, into Thursday morning.

The Orionids are debris from Halley's Comet that streak across the sky as comets every fall.

The Orionid meteor shower is the strongest meteor shower in October. The weaker Draconid meteor shower takes place earlier in the month.

The Orionids, which are active between Oct. 2 and Nov. 7, will peak overnight on Oct. 21-22, when around 10 to 20 meteors should be visible if the skies remain clear and dark, according to Space.com.

"However, a bright waxing gibbous moon will make viewing a little trickier this year, washing out fainter shooting stars. BUT don't give up on the Orionids just yet. These meteors are known for their incredible speed and bright glowing trails," Space.com said.

Where to watch meteor showers in Nevada

For the clearest views, there are several places that are an easy drive from Reno where you can get a clear view of the stars, including:

  • Lake Tahoe: Multiple locations around the lake are excellent for stargazing and are less than an hour from Reno.
  • Fort Churchill State Park: The park on Alt. 95 south of Silver Springs provides a dark night sky ideal for evening astronomical events among the ruins of Fort Churchill. Park entrance costs $5 for Nevada residents and $10 for non-residents.
  • Pyramid Lake: A popular spot for Renoites seeking a night of stargazing, the lake is less than an hour from The Biggest Little City. It offers beautiful natural wonders and dark skies that give a clear view of lunar eclipses, meteor showers, and full moons.

Meteor showers over Nevada for the remainder of 2026

Below are the peaks of four remaining meteor showers visible in the Northern Hemisphere in 2026, with their visual strength ratings courtesy of Britannica.com:

  • Nov. 11-12: Taurid meteor shower (weak)
  • Nov. 16-17: Leonid meteor shower (irregular)
  • Dec. 13-14: Geminid meteor shower (strong)
  • Dec. 21-22: Ursid meteor shower (medium)

Dates for 2026's remaining full moons

Skywatchers can catch three more full moons in 2026. Some astronomers consider two of them "supermoons," when the moon's orbit is closest to Earth during a full moon (though there's no strict definition of how close the moon needs to be to be declared a supermoon). These will be in November and December to close out the year.

Here are the dates for the remaining three full moons in 2026:

  • Oct. 26: Hunter’s Moon
  • Nov. 24: Beaver Moon
  • Dec. 24: Cold Moon
